• [color=#991B1B]IV epinephrine bolus is NOT routine treatment for anaphylaxis and carries significant risk. Use IV infusion only in appropriate monitored settings with experienced clinicians when indicated.[/color]

[color=#1E3A8A]C. Respiratory Paralysis and Shock[/color]
• Secure airway and provide assisted ventilation when indicated. Treat shock with carefully reassessed IV fluids and vasopressors when necessary. Monitor urine output and renal function. Treat clinically significant bleeding and coagulopathy with specialist guidance; antivenom is primary venom-specific treatment when indicated.

sections.heading: 05 — DISPOSITION
sections.content:
• Admit patients with suspected envenomation for serial clinical and laboratory assessment.
• ICU care indicated for respiratory weakness, bulbar dysfunction, shock, significant bleeding, severe coagulopathy, or acute kidney injury.
• Arrange follow-up for delayed bleeding, renal complications, tissue injury, and serum sickness after antivenom when relevant.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: WHO Snakebite Envenoming: Treatment and Prevention; WHO regional guidelines; Goldfrank's; Current regional antivenom product information.

sections.heading: 01 — RECOGNIZE
sections.content:
Scorpion venom may cause severe autonomic stimulation, neuromuscular symptoms, cardiopulmonary complications. Severity depends on species, amount of venom, patient age, time to treatment.

[color=#1E3A8A]Local:[/color] Severe pain or burning. Paresthesia, tingling, local swelling.
[color=#1E3A8A]Systemic:[/color] Sweating, agitation, vomiting, excessive salivation. Tachycardia or hypertension. Muscle twitching or abnormal eye movements. Respiratory distress or excessive airway secretions. Pulmonary edema, myocardial dysfunction, or shock in severe envenomation.
• Children may deteriorate more rapidly than adults.

sections.heading: 02 — IMMEDIATE ACTIONS
sections.content:
• Ensure patient in safe environment. Assess ABCs and vital signs.
• Establish IV access for systemic symptoms. Monitor ECG and SpO2 when systemic toxicity suspected.
• Provide local wound care.
• Contact toxicology or regional envenomation service for severe symptoms and species-specific treatment advice.

sections.heading: 03 — INVESTIGATIONS
sections.content:
• ECG and continuous cardiac monitoring in systemic toxicity.
• Blood gas and lactate in respiratory distress or shock. Electrolytes, renal function, glucose.
• Troponin and echocardiography when myocardial injury or dysfunction suspected. Chest imaging for suspected pulmonary edema.

sections.heading: 04 — TREATMENT
sections.content:
[color=#1E3A8A]A. Local Pain Control[/color]
• Use appropriate analgesia according to age, weight, contraindications, local protocols. Clean sting site. Apply cool compress if appropriate; avoid ice-related tissue injury. Reassess pain and monitor for evolving systemic symptoms.
• [color=#991B1B]Do NOT cut, suck, burn, or apply tight tourniquet to sting site. Avoid local anesthetic techniques unless performed by clinician familiar with relevant anatomy and indications.[/color]

[color=#1E3A8A]B. Antivenom[/color]
• Indication: Use antivenom only when effective against local scorpion species and patient meets regional treatment criteria. Severe systemic manifestations, particularly in children, require urgent specialist assessment.
• Dose: Follow exact product-specific regional protocol. Do NOT assume antivenom products for different scorpion species are interchangeable.
• [color=#991B1B]Antivenom efficacy and indications differ by region and product. Do NOT delay airway support or treatment of shock while obtaining antivenom.[/color]

[color=#1E3A8A]C. Severe Autonomic or Cardiovascular Toxicity[/color]
• Provide oxygen and ventilatory support as needed. Treat shock with careful fluid assessment and specialist-directed vasoactive therapy. Manage pulmonary edema and myocardial dysfunction in ICU. In selected regional syndromes, prazosin or other specific treatment may be recommended by local protocols.
• [color=#991B1B]Do NOT give prazosin routinely to every scorpion-sting patient. Its use depends on local species, clinical syndrome, hemodynamic state, regional evidence. Avoid excessive fluid administration when myocardial dysfunction or pulmonary edema present.[/color]

sections.heading: 05 — DISPOSITION
sections.content:
• Observe patients according to local species-specific guidance.
• Admit patients with systemic symptoms, abnormal vital signs, significant pain requiring repeated parenteral treatment, or relevant pediatric risk.
• ICU care indicated for respiratory failure, pulmonary edema, shock, or myocardial dysfunction.

sections.heading: 06 — OTHER DANGEROUS BITES
sections.content:
For bites from mammals, bats, or other animals, assess separately for:
• Wound infection and tissue injury.
• Rabies exposure and need for post-exposure prophylaxis.
• Tetanus immunization status.
• Indications for antibiotics, surgical exploration, or specialist review.
• Do NOT assume all animal bites require antibiotics, and do NOT delay rabies assessment when a potentially rabid animal was involved.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: WHO Guidelines for Management of Snakebites and Other Envenoming; Goldfrank's; Regional scorpion antivenom guidance.

E. Environmental and Special Toxicology.title: Toxicologic Cardiac Arrest and Refractory Shock

sections.heading: 01 — RECOGNIZE
sections.content:
Toxicologic cardiac arrest occurs when a drug or chemical causes severe hypoxia, myocardial depression, dysrhythmia, or circulatory collapse.

[color=#1E3A8A]Potential causes:[/color] Sodium-channel blocker toxicity (e.g., TCAs). Beta-blocker or calcium-channel blocker overdose. Digoxin toxicity. Opioid-induced respiratory arrest. Cyanide or severe toxic alcohol poisoning. Local anesthetic systemic toxicity. Severe hyperkalemia or other toxic-metabolic disturbances.
• [color=#991B1B]IMPORTANT: Standard resuscitation remains essential, but selected poisonings require specific antidotes and modified treatment strategies.[/color]

sections.heading: 02 — IMMEDIATE ACTIONS
sections.content:
• Confirm cardiac arrest and activate resuscitation team. Start high-quality CPR immediately.
• Apply defibrillator pads and identify rhythm. Provide oxygenation and ventilation while avoiding excessive ventilation.
• Establish IV or intraosseous access. Check bedside glucose and consider reversible metabolic causes.
• Obtain focused exposure history from witnesses, medication containers, or records.
• Identify and administer relevant antidote when indicated.
• Contact toxicology and critical care early. Consider extracorporeal CPR or other advanced rescue options in selected refractory cases where available.

sections.heading: 03 — INVESTIGATIONS
sections.content:
During resuscitation, obtain tests when they do not interrupt CPR:
• Blood gas, pH, lactate, electrolytes. Potassium, glucose, renal function.
• ECG and rhythm analysis. Specific drug concentrations when available and clinically useful.
• Echocardiography during appropriate pauses or after ROSC. Evaluation for co-ingestion and additional reversible causes.

sections.heading: 04 — TREATMENT
sections.content:
[color=#1E3A8A]A. Standard Resuscitation[/color]
• Follow current adult/pediatric advanced life support algorithm. For adult cardiac arrest, epinephrine commonly 1 mg IV/IO every 3–5 minutes per applicable algorithm. Defibrillation energy and medication selection depend on rhythm and current protocol.
• [color=#991B1B]Standard resuscitation is necessary but may be insufficient without toxin-specific treatment. Avoid unstructured administration of multiple antidotes without plausible toxicologic indication.[/color]

[color=#1E3A8A]B. Sodium Bicarbonate for Sodium-Channel Blocker Toxicity[/color]
• Indication: Suspected sodium-channel blocker poisoning with QRS widening, ventricular dysrhythmia, or hemodynamic instability, particularly with TCAs or selected other agents.
• Commonly used initial dose: 1–2 mEq/kg IV. Repeat according to ECG response, hemodynamics, blood gas, and institutional toxicology protocol.
• [color=#991B1B]Bicarbonate is NOT a universal antidote for every toxicologic arrest. Use for appropriate indications and monitor response.[/color]

[color=#1E3A8A]C. High-Dose Insulin Euglycemia Therapy[/color]
• Indication: Consider for severe beta-blocker or calcium-channel blocker poisoning with myocardial dysfunction or refractory shock, under specialist-led critical care protocols.
• Commonly used starting regimen: Regular insulin 1 unit/kg IV bolus, then 1 unit/kg/hour IV infusion, with escalation according to hemodynamic response and institutional protocol. Doses may require substantial escalation in severe poisoning, but must occur under dedicated high-dose insulin protocol.
• [color=#991B1B]High-dose insulin therapy can cause severe and delayed hypoglycemia and hypokalemia. Requires trained staff, frequent laboratory testing, and standardized protocol. Do NOT initiate without clear indication and appropriate monitoring capability.[/color]

[color=#1E3A8A]D. Lipid Emulsion Therapy[/color]
• Indication: Consider 20% lipid emulsion for severe local anesthetic systemic toxicity and selected other highly lipophilic drug poisonings when recommended by relevant toxicology protocol.
• For adult LAST: 20% lipid emulsion 1.5 mL/kg IV bolus, followed by 0.25 mL/kg/min infusion. If instability persists, repeat bolus and increase infusion per current local checklist. Use ASRA checklist or equivalent for exact dosing, duration, maximum cumulative dose.
• [color=#991B1B]Lipid emulsion is NOT recommended routinely for every poisoning or cardiac arrest. Avoid indiscriminate administration because it may cause complications and interfere with lab testing or extracorporeal circuits.[/color]

[color=#1E3A8A]E. Calcium for Calcium-Channel Blocker Toxicity[/color]
• Indication: Use IV calcium for clinically significant CCB poisoning with hypotension, bradycardia, or myocardial dysfunction, per local protocol.
• Calcium chloride 10% or calcium gluconate 10% may be used; volume differs because elemental calcium content differs. Select preparation and dose according to clinical situation and institutional toxicology protocol.
• [color=#991B1B]Avoid extravasation and monitor for hypercalcemia. Calcium is an adjunct and must NOT delay high-dose insulin or vasopressors when indicated.[/color]

[color=#1E3A8A]F. Toxin-Specific Antidotes[/color]
• Choose antidote according to suspected cause: Opioid toxicity: naloxone + ventilation. Cyanide poisoning: hydroxocobalamin. Digoxin toxicity: digoxin immune Fab. LAST: lipid emulsion per ASRA checklist. Beta-blocker/CCB toxicity: high-dose insulin and other specialist-directed therapies. Toxic alcohol poisoning: fomepizole and hemodialysis when indicated. Isoniazid poisoning with seizures: pyridoxine.
• [color=#991B1B]Antidotes are NOT interchangeable. Use relevant poisoning-specific protocol and involve toxicology early.[/color]

[color=#1E3A8A]G. Refractory Shock and Extracorporeal Support[/color]
• Indications for specialist consideration: Persistent shock despite appropriate antidotes, fluids, vasopressors, toxin-specific therapies. Refractory cardiogenic shock from selected beta-blocker or CCB poisonings. Selected cases of severe cardiotoxic drug poisoning where recovery possible and local resources permit.
• [color=#991B1B]ECMO and extracorporeal CPR require specialized teams and patient selection. They are NOT substitutes for immediate CPR, defibrillation, or indicated antidotes.[/color]

sections.heading: 05 — POST-RESUSCITATION CARE
sections.content: • Secure airway and optimize ventilation/oxygenation. Treat shock and monitor cardiac function. Correct glucose/electrolyte abnormalities. Repeat blood gas, lactate, relevant toxin levels. Evaluate for hypoxic brain injury and other complications. Continue treatment for underlying poisoning and assess for recurrent toxicity.

sections.heading: 06 — DISPOSITION
sections.content:
• ICU admission required after toxicologic cardiac arrest or severe refractory shock.
• Continue monitoring for recurrent dysrhythmia, delayed hypoglycemia, rebound toxicity, organ injury.
• Arrange specialist follow-up and document suspected agent, antidotes, response, complications.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: AHA 2025 Guidelines; ASRA LAST Checklist; EXTRIP Workgroup Recommendations; Goldfrank's.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Cardiac Arrest, Anaphylaxis, Severe Asthma, Shock, Symptomatic Bradycardia.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Cardiac Arrest:[/b] 1 mg IV/IO every 3-5 mins.
• [b]Anaphylaxis:[/b] 0.5 mg IM (1:1000).
• [b]Bradycardia/Shock:[/b] 0.05–0.5 mcg/kg/min IV infusion.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Cardiac Arrest:[/b] 0.01 mg/kg IV/IO (max 1 mg).
• [b]Anaphylaxis:[/b] 0.01 mg/kg IM (max 0.5 mg).
• [b]Bradycardia/Shock:[/b] 0.05–0.3 mcg/kg/min IV infusion.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Beta-blockers:[/b] May cause unopposed alpha-adrenergic effects (severe hypertension).
• [b]MAOIs / TCAs:[/b] Enhances the pressor effect (risk of hypertensive crisis).
• [b]Halogenated Anesthetics:[/b] Increases risk of ventricular arrhythmias.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Tachycardia, palpitations, arrhythmias (VT/VF).
• Severe hypertension, myocardial ischemia.
• Anxiety, tremor, headache.
• Tissue necrosis at extravasation site.
• Hyperglycemia.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]NEVER give IV bolus of 1:1000 (1 mg/mL) in anaphylaxis — fatal error.[/color]
• High-alert medication; requires independent double-check.
• Extravasation causes severe tissue injury (use Phentolamine).
• Use central line for prolonged infusions.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Crosses the placenta.
• [b]Effect on fetus:[/b] May decrease uterine blood flow and cause fetal tachycardia.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk in small amounts. Use with caution.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: AHA 2025 Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Septic Shock, Cardiogenic Shock, Neurogenic Shock.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.05–0.5 mcg/kg/min IV infusion, titrated to MAP ≥ 65 mmHg.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.05–0.3 mcg/kg/min IV infusion, titrated to age-appropriate BP.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]MAOIs / TCAs:[/b] Severe hypertension.
• [b]Cocaine:[/b] Additive hypertensive effect.
• [b]Beta-blockers:[/b] May cause reflex bradycardia.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Hypertension, reflex bradycardia, arrhythmias.
• Myocardial ischemia, peripheral ischemia.
• Tissue necrosis at extravasation site.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Extravasation causes severe tissue necrosis (use Phentolamine).[/color]
• Central venous access preferred.
• Do not stop infusion abruptly (reduce gradually).

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. May decrease uterine blood flow.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown if excreted in breast milk. Use with caution.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Septic Shock (second-line), Variceal Bleeding, Diabetes Insipidus.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Septic Shock:[/b] 0.03 units/min (fixed rate, no titration).
• [b]Variceal Bleeding:[/b] 0.2–0.4 units/min IV infusion.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Vasodilatory Shock:[/b] 0.0005–0.002 units/kg/min IV infusion.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Corticosteroids:[/b] May increase fluid retention and risk of hyponatremia.
• [b]Other Vasopressors:[/b] Additive effect (may need to reduce norepinephrine dose).

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Ischemia (digital, mesenteric, myocardial).
• Hyponatremia (water intoxication).
• Bradycardia, arrhythmias.
• Abdominal cramps, nausea.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• High-alert medication.
• [color=#991B1B]Risk of severe ischemia, especially in patients with cardiovascular disease.[/color]
• Do not use as a bolus push for shock (only IV infusion).

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Oxytocic effect (may stimulate uterine contractions). Use with caution.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk, but minimal effect.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Cardiogenic Shock, Acute Heart Failure with low cardiac output.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 2.5–20 mcg/kg/min IV infusion.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 2–20 mcg/kg/min IV infusion.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Beta-blockers:[/b] Antagonize the inotropic effect of dobutamine.
• [b]MAOIs:[/b] Enhances the pressor effect.
• [b]Nitrates / Vasodilators:[/b] Additive hypotension.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Tachycardia, arrhythmias (VT, AFib).
• Hypotension (due to vasodilation).
• Headache, tremor, anxiety.
• Myocardial ischemia (increased oxygen demand).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]May worsen hypotension in patients with low preload.[/color]
• Do NOT give as a routine IV bolus.
• Monitor ECG and BP continuously.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. May cause fetal tachycardia.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown if excreted in breast milk.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: ESC 2021 Heart Failure Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Symptomatic Bradycardia, Shock (less common now).

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Bradycardia/Shock:[/b] 5–20 mcg/kg/min IV infusion.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 5–20 mcg/kg/min IV infusion.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]MAOIs:[/b] Severe hypertension.
• [b]Phenytoin:[/b] May cause hypotension and bradycardia.
• [b]Beta-blockers:[/b] Antagonize cardiac effects.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Tachyarrhythmias, hypertension.
• Myocardial ischemia, angina.
• Nausea, vomiting.
• Tissue necrosis at extravasation site.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Higher arrhythmia risk than norepinephrine (not first-line).[/color]
• Extravasation causes severe tissue necrosis (use Phentolamine).
• Do not mix with sodium bicarbonate.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Decreases uterine blood flow.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown if excreted in breast milk.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: AHA 2025 Bradycardia Algorithm; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Hypotension (especially with tachycardia).

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Bolus:[/b] 40–100 mcg IV.
• [b]Infusion:[/b] 0.1–1 mcg/kg/min IV.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 5–20 mcg/kg IV bolus.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]MAOIs / TCAs:[/b] Severe hypertension.
• [b]Beta-blockers:[/b] May cause severe hypertension and reflex bradycardia.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Reflex bradycardia.
• Hypertension, myocardial ischemia.
• Headache, anxiety, tremor.
• Tissue necrosis at extravasation site.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Use with caution in patients with heart failure or bradycardia.[/color]
• Extravasation causes severe tissue necrosis.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. May reduce uterine blood flow.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown if excreted in breast milk.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF; Local Anesthesia Guidelines.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Hypotension (especially during spinal anesthesia).

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 5–10 mg IV (max 50 mg).

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.2–0.3 mg/kg IV.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]MAOIs:[/b] Severe hypertensive crisis (contraindicated).
• [b]Oxytocin:[/b] Severe hypertension if used together.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Tachycardia, hypertension, arrhythmias.
• Anxiety, tremor, insomnia.
• Urinary retention.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Tachyphylaxis (rapid tolerance) develops quickly.[/color]
• Avoid in tachyarrhythmias or severe CAD.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. May cause fetal tachycardia.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk in small amounts.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF; Local Anesthesia Guidelines.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Cardiac Arrest (VF/pVT), Stable VT, Atrial Fibrillation.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Cardiac Arrest:[/b] 300 mg IV/IO rapid push (1st), 150 mg (2nd).
• [b]Stable VT:[/b] 150 mg IV over 10 mins, then 1 mg/min x 6h, 0.5 mg/min x 18h.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Cardiac Arrest:[/b] 5 mg/kg IV/IO bolus (max 300 mg).
• [b]Stable VT:[/b] 5 mg/kg IV over 20-60 mins (max 300 mg).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Warfarin:[/b] Increases INR (risk of bleeding).
• [b]Digoxin:[/b] Increases digoxin levels.
• [b]Beta-blockers / CCBs:[/b] Risk of bradycardia and AV block.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Bradycardia, hypotension, AV block.
• QT prolongation.
• Thyroid dysfunction, pulmonary toxicity (long-term), hepatotoxicity.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]MUST dilute in 5% Dextrose (precipitates in saline).[/color]
• High risk of hypotension if pushed too fast.
• Avoid in 2nd/3rd-degree AV block without pacing.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category D. Can cause fetal thyroid dysfunction and bradycardia.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Use with caution.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: AHA 2025; ESC 2019; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Ventricular Arrhythmias (VT/VF), Local Anesthesia.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Cardiac Arrest:[/b] 1–1.5 mg/kg IV/IO (1st), 0.5–0.75 mg/kg (2nd).
• [b]Stable VT:[/b] 1–1.5 mg/kg IV bolus, then 1–4 mg/min infusion.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 1 mg/kg IV/IO bolus (for VT/VF).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Cimetidine / Beta-blockers:[/b] Increase lidocaine levels (risk of toxicity).
• [b]Phenytoin:[/b] May alter lidocaine levels.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• CNS toxicity: Dizziness, confusion, seizures, coma.
• Bradycardia, hypotension, arrhythmias.
• Nausea, metallic taste.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Reduce dose in hepatic impairment.[/color]
• Do not use with epinephrine in digits.
• Monitor for signs of CNS toxicity.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. May cause fetal bradycardia if high doses used.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk in small amounts.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: AHA 2025 ACLS Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Symptomatic Bradycardia, Organophosphate Poisoning.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Bradycardia:[/b] 1 mg IV q3-5min (max 3 mg).
• [b]Organophosphate:[/b] 2-5 mg IV, double every 5-10 mins.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Bradycardia:[/b] 0.02 mg/kg IV (min 0.1 mg, max 0.5 mg).
• [b]Organophosphate:[/b] 0.05 mg/kg IV.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Other anticholinergics:[/b] Additive toxicity.
• [b]MAOIs / TCAs:[/b] Additive anticholinergic effects.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Tachycardia, arrhythmias.
• Dry mouth, blurred vision, urinary retention.
• Confusion, delirium (elderly).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]AVOID in infranodal blocks (Mobitz II, 3rd-degree AV block).[/color]
• Minimum pediatric dose 0.1 mg (paradoxical bradycardia if too low).

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. May cause fetal tachycardia.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk (may decrease milk production).

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: AHA 2025 Bradycardia Algorithm; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Stable Narrow-Complex Regular Tachycardia (SVT).

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 6 mg rapid IV push (1st). If ineffective, 12 mg rapid IV push (2nd).

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.1 mg/kg rapid IV push (max 6 mg). If ineffective, 0.2 mg/kg (max 12 mg).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Dipyridamole:[/b] Enhances the effect (reduce dose).
• [b]Carbamazepine:[/b] Enhances AV block.
• [b]Caffeine / Theophylline:[/b] Antagonize the effect.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Flushing, chest pain, dyspnea.
• Bronchospasm (dangerous in asthmatics).
• Transient asystole, bradycardia.
• Headache, dizziness.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Contraindicated in Asthma/COPD (can cause severe bronchospasm).[/color]
• Contraindicated in irregular or wide-complex tachycardia.
• Use a proximal IV and rapid saline flush (half-life < 10 seconds).

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. May cause fetal bradycardia.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown if excreted in breast milk.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: AHA 2025 Tachycardia Algorithm; ESC 2019 SVT Guidelines.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Severe Asthma, Eclampsia/Preeclampsia, Torsades de Pointes.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Asthma:[/b] 1.2–2 g IV over 20 mins.
• [b]Eclampsia:[/b] 4 g IV loading, then 1 g/hour infusion.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Asthma:[/b] 25–50 mg/kg IV (max 2 g) over 20 mins.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Neuromuscular Blockers:[/b] Enhances the effect (risk of prolonged paralysis).
• [b]CCBs:[/b] Additive hypotension.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Flushing, sweating, hypotension.
• Loss of deep tendon reflexes (early toxicity).
• Respiratory depression, coma (severe toxicity).
• Hypocalcemia.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]MONITOR: Deep tendon reflexes, respiratory rate (>12/min), urine output (>30 mL/h).[/color]
• [b]Antidote:[/b] Calcium Gluconate 10% 10 mL IV.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Used routinely for eclampsia.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Use with caution.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: GINA 2024; NICE NG133.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Hyperkalemia, Hypocalcemia, Magnesium Toxicity.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Hyperkalemia:[/b] 10–30 mL of 10% solution IV over 10 mins.
• [b]Hypocalcemia:[/b] 10–20 mL of 10% solution IV.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.5–1 mL/kg of 10% solution IV (max 20 mL).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Ceftriaxone:[/b] Risk of precipitation in neonates.
• [b]Digoxin:[/b] Risk of digoxin toxicity (calcium can potentiate).

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Bradycardia, arrhythmias (if given too fast).
• Hypotension.
• Tissue necrosis if extravasation occurs.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Do NOT mix with Sodium Bicarbonate (precipitates).[/color]
• Administer slowly (max 3-5 mL/min) via a large vein.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: UK Kidney Association Guidelines.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Cardiac Arrest (Hyperkalemia, CCB toxicity), Hypocalcemia.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 5–10 mL of 10% solution IV slowly.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.1–0.2 mL/kg of 10% solution IV (max 10 mL).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • Same as Calcium Gluconate (Ceftriaxone, Digoxin, Thiazides).

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Severe tissue necrosis if extravasation.
• Bradycardia, arrhythmias.
• Metabolic acidosis.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Highly irritating; requires central venous access if possible.[/color]
• Contains 3 times more elemental calcium than Calcium Gluconate.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: AHA 2025 ACLS Guidelines.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Hypertensive Emergency, Aortic Dissection.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]IV Bolus:[/b] 20 mg over 2 mins, then 40–80 mg every 10 mins (max 300 mg total).
• [b]IV Infusion:[/b] 0.5–2 mg/min.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.2–1 mg/kg IV (max 40 mg/dose).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]CCBs:[/b] Risk of AV block and bradycardia.
• [b]MAOIs:[/b] Hypertensive crisis.
• [b]Cimetidine:[/b] Increases labetalol levels.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Bradycardia, hypotension, heart block.
• Bronchospasm (especially in asthmatics).
• Scalp tingling, fatigue, dizziness.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Contraindicated in severe asthma, heart block, or decompensated heart failure.[/color]
• Do not use in cocaine-induced hypertension.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Drug of choice for pregnancy-induced hypertension.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk in small amounts. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: NICE NG133; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Hypertensive Emergency (pregnancy), Acute Heart Failure.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 5–10 mg IV slowly over 20 mins. Repeat every 20-30 mins.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.1–0.2 mg/kg IV (max 20 mg).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]MAOIs:[/b] Severe hypotension.
• [b]NSAIDs:[/b] Decreased antihypertensive effect.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Reflex tachycardia, angina, headache.
• Hypotension.
• Lupus-like syndrome (with long-term use).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Unpredictable hypotensive effect; monitor BP closely.[/color]
• Avoid in severe tachycardia or aortic dissection.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Safe in pregnancy for HTN.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: NICE NG133; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Pulmonary Edema, Fluid Overload, Hypertensive Emergency.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]IV:[/b] 20–40 mg slowly (naive), or 1-2.5x oral dose (chronic). Max rate 4 mg/min.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.5–2 mg/kg IV (max 40 mg).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]NSAIDs:[/b] Decreased diuretic effect.
• [b]Aminoglycosides:[/b] Increased ototoxicity.
• [b]Digoxin:[/b] Hypokalemia increases digoxin toxicity.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hypovolemia.
• Ototoxicity (tinnitus, deafness).
• Acute kidney injury (AKI).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Administer slowly (max 4 mg/min) to avoid ototoxicity.[/color]
• Monitor electrolytes, renal function, and urine output.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Crosses placenta.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk (may decrease milk production).

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: ESC 2021 Heart Failure Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] ACS (STEMI/NSTEMI), Secondary prevention.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]ACS:[/b] 162–325 mg PO (chewed), then 75–100 mg daily.
• [b]Secondary Prevention:[/b] 75–81 mg daily.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Kawasaki Disease:[/b] 80–100 mg/kg/day divided.
• [color=#991B1B]CONTRAINDICATED in children with viral illness (Reye's syndrome).[/color]

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Anticoagulants / NSAIDs:[/b] Increased risk of GI bleeding.
• [b]Ibuprofen:[/b] Antagonizes the antiplatelet effect.
• [b]Methotrexate:[/b] Increased toxicity.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• GI irritation, peptic ulcer, upper GI bleeding.
• Bronchospasm.
• Tinnitus, hearing loss (high doses).
• Hypersensitivity reactions.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]NEVER give to children/teenagers with fever/viral illness.[/color]
• Contraindicated in active bleeding or severe aspirin allergy.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category D (3rd trimester). Low-dose safe for preeclampsia. High doses cause premature closure of ductus arteriosus.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Avoid high doses.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: ESC 2023 ACS Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] ACS (DAPT with Aspirin), Post-PCI, Secondary prevention.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]ACS/PCI:[/b] 300–600 mg PO loading, then 75 mg PO daily.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• Rarely used; specialist use only.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Omeprazole/Esomeprazole:[/b] Reduce clopidogrel activation (use Pantoprazole).
• [b]Anticoagulants / NSAIDs:[/b] Increased risk of bleeding.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Bleeding (GI, intracranial, bruising).
• Diarrhea, abdominal pain.
• Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP - rare).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]CYP2C19 poor metabolizers may have reduced efficacy.[/color]
• Contraindicated in active pathological bleeding.
• Do not discontinue prematurely after PCI.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Use only if clearly needed.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown if excreted in breast milk.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: ESC 2023 ACS Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] ACS, Venous Thromboembolism (VTE), Hemodialysis.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]ACS:[/b] 60 units/kg IV bolus (max 4000 units), then 12 units/kg/hr infusion.
• [b]VTE:[/b] 80 units/kg bolus, then 18 units/kg/hr infusion.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Infant (<1 yr):[/b] 75 units/kg bolus, then 28 units/kg/hr.
• [b]Child (>1 yr):[/b] 75 units/kg bolus, then 20 units/kg/hr.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Antiplatelets / NSAIDs:[/b] Increased bleeding risk.
• [b]Nitroglycerin:[/b] Can reduce heparin activity.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Bleeding, bruising, hematoma.
• Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT).
• Hyperkalemia.
• Osteoporosis (long-term use).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Monitor platelets daily (risk of HIT).[/color]
• [b]Antidote:[/b] Protamine Sulfate (1 mg per 100 units of heparin).

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Does NOT cross the placenta (safe for fetus).
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Not excreted in breast milk (large molecule). Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: ACCP Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] VTE Prophylaxis/Treatment, ACS.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Prophylaxis:[/b] 40 mg SC once daily.
• [b]Treatment:[/b] 1 mg/kg SC every 12 hours.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Treatment:[/b] 1 mg/kg SC every 12 hours.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • Same as Unfractionated Heparin.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Bleeding (less than UFH).
• HIT (rare).
• Injection site hematoma.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Reduce dose in severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30).[/color]
• [b]Antidote:[/b] Protamine Sulfate (partially effective).

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Preferred anticoagulant in pregnancy.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Not excreted in breast milk. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: ACCP Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Acute Ischemic Stroke, STEMI, Massive PE.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Stroke:[/b] 0.9 mg/kg IV (max 90 mg). 10% bolus, rest over 60 mins.
• [b]STEMI:[/b] 15 mg bolus, 0.75 mg/kg over 30 mins, then 0.5 mg/kg over 60 mins.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• Specialized use only.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Anticoagulants / Antiplatelets:[/b] Severe bleeding risk.
• [b]ACE inhibitors:[/b] Increased risk of angioedema.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Severe bleeding (Intracranial hemorrhage).
• Reperfusion arrhythmias.
• Allergic reactions.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]STRICT contraindications: Recent stroke, ICH, recent surgery, uncontrolled BP.[/color]
• Monitor for neurological deterioration.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Risk of maternal hemorrhage.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: AHA/ASA Stroke Guidelines; ESC 2023.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Trauma Hemorrhage, Postpartum Hemorrhage.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 1 g IV over 10 mins, then 1 g IV infusion over 8 hours.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 15 mg/kg IV (max 1 g) over 10 mins, then 2 mg/kg/hr for 8 hours.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Prothrombotic agents:[/b] Increased risk of thrombosis.
• [b]Anticoagulants:[/b] Antagonizes their effect.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea.
• Thromboembolism (rare but serious).
• Seizures (high doses).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Give within 3 hours of trauma.[/color]
• Reduce dose in renal impairment.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Safe (used for PPH).
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk in very small amounts. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: CRASH-2 Trial; WOMAN Trial; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Reversal of Unfractionated Heparin (UFH).

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 1 mg neutralizes 100 units of heparin. Give 25–50 mg IV slowly over 10 mins.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• Same ratio.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Blood products:[/b] Can interact.
• [b]NPH insulin:[/b] Risk of severe allergic reaction.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Severe hypotension and bradycardia.
• Anaphylaxis.
• Pulmonary hypertension.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Administer SLOWLY (max 5 mg/min).[/color]
• Have epinephrine ready.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: ACCP Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Reversal of Warfarin, Vitamin K deficiency.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Warfarin Reversal:[/b] 1–5 mg PO/IV (major bleeding: 5–10 mg IV).

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Deficiency bleeding:[/b] 1 mg IV (0.5 mg if < 1 year).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]Warfarin:[/b] Directly antagonizes its effect.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Anaphylactoid reactions (rare, with rapid IV push).
• Injection site pain.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]IV administration should be very slow.[/color]
• Prefer Oral/SC route if not life-threatening.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Safe (standard at birth).
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BCSH Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Asthma, COPD Exacerbation, Hyperkalemia.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Nebulized:[/b] 2.5–5 mg every 20 mins.
• [b]MDI:[/b] 4–10 puffs every 20 mins.
• [b]IV:[/b] 5–20 mcg/min.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Nebulized:[/b] 2.5 mg (<5 yrs) or 5 mg (>5 yrs) every 20 mins.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Non-selective Beta-blockers:[/b] Antagonize bronchodilator effect.
• [b]Diuretics:[/b] Increased risk of hypokalemia.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Tachycardia, palpitations, arrhythmias.
• Fine tremor.
• Hypokalemia and hyperglycemia.
• Lactic acidosis.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]High doses can cause dangerous tachyarrhythmias and lactic acidosis.[/color]
• Monitor K+ levels.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Safe for acute asthma.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: GINA 2024; BTS/SIGN Guidelines.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Severe Asthma, COPD Exacerbation.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Nebulized:[/b] 0.5 mg every 4-6 hours.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Nebulized:[/b] 0.25 mg (<5 years) or 0.5 mg (>5 years).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • No significant interactions. Can be mixed with salbutamol.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Dry mouth, bitter taste.
• Urinary retention (rare).
• Glaucoma exacerbation.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]Avoid contact with eyes (risk of acute angle-closure glaucoma).[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Safe.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown if excreted in breast milk.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: GINA 2024; GOLD 2024.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Asthma (maintenance), Croup (nebulized).

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Asthma:[/b] Inhaled 200–800 mcg BID.
• [b]Nebulized:[/b] 1–2 mg BID.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Croup:[/b] 2 mg nebulized as a single dose.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]CYP3A4 inhibitors:[/b] Increase systemic levels of budesonide.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Oral candidiasis (thrush).
• Dysphonia.
• Adrenal suppression (high doses).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Rinse mouth with water after inhalation to prevent oral thrush.[/color]
• Do not use as a rescue inhaler.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Inhaled budesonide is safe.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk in minimal amounts. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: GINA 2024; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Severe Asthma, COPD (rarely used now).

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Loading Dose:[/b] 5 mg/kg IV over 20 mins (omit if on oral theophylline).
• [b]Maintenance:[/b] 0.5 mg/kg/hour IV infusion.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Loading Dose:[/b] 5–10 mg/kg IV over 20 mins.
• [b]Maintenance:[/b] 0.5–1 mg/kg/hour IV infusion.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Ciprofloxacin / Erythromycin:[/b] Increase aminophylline levels (risk of toxicity).
• [b]Phenytoin / Rifampicin:[/b] Decrease aminophylline levels.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Tachycardia, arrhythmias.
• Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain.
• Seizures (sign of severe toxicity).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Very narrow therapeutic window. Monitor theophylline levels if possible.[/color]
• Reduce dose in heart failure or liver disease.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Crosses placenta.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: GINA 2024; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Acute Asthma (SC), Tocolysis.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]SC:[/b] 0.25–0.5 mg (max 1 mg in 24h).
• [b]Nebulized:[/b] 5–10 mg.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]SC:[/b] 0.01 mg/kg (max 0.3 mg).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Beta-blockers:[/b] Antagonize effect.
• [b]Corticosteroids:[/b] Increased risk of hypokalemia.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Tachycardia, palpitations, tremor.
• Hypokalemia.
• Pulmonary edema (prolonged tocolysis).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]Prolonged use as a tocolytic is contraindicated (risk of maternal pulmonary edema).[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Used with strict monitoring.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: GINA 2024; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Adrenal Crisis, Anaphylaxis (adjunct), Severe Asthma.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Adrenal Crisis:[/b] 100–200 mg IV bolus, then 50–100 mg q6h.
• [b]Asthma:[/b] 100–200 mg IV q6h.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Adrenal Crisis:[/b] 2–4 mg/kg IV bolus, then 2–4 mg/kg q6h.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]NSAIDs:[/b] Increased risk of GI ulceration.
• [b]Live vaccines:[/b] Contraindicated.
• [b]Insulin:[/b] Corticosteroids raise blood glucose.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Hyperglycemia, fluid retention, hypertension.
• Hypokalemia.
• Immunosuppression.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Do not stop abruptly if used for > 2 weeks (risk of adrenal crisis).[/color]
• Watch for signs of infection.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Safe when indicated.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk in small amounts. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Severe Asthma/COPD, MS relapse.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Asthma/COPD:[/b] 40–125 mg IV q6-8h.
• [b]MS Relapse:[/b] 1 g IV daily for 3-5 days.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Asthma:[/b] 1–2 mg/kg IV daily (max 60 mg).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • Similar to Hydrocortisone.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Hyperglycemia, hypertension, fluid retention.
• Psychosis, insomnia.
• Peptic ulcer disease.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]High doses can cause arrhythmias (especially IV push).[/color]
• Administer slowly.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: GINA 2024; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Croup (Pediatric), Meningitis, Cerebral Edema.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Meningitis:[/b] 10 mg IV q6h.
• [b]Cerebral Edema:[/b] 10 mg IV bolus, then 4 mg q6h.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Croup:[/b] 0.15–0.6 mg/kg PO/IV (max 10 mg) single dose.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Antidiabetics:[/b] Dexamethasone raises blood sugar.
• [b]Phenytoin / Rifampicin:[/b] Decrease steroid effect.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Hyperglycemia, hypertension.
• GI upset.
• Hiccups, insomnia, mood changes.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Do NOT use steroids in traumatic brain injury.[/color]
• Give before or with first dose of antibiotics in meningitis.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Used for fetal lung maturity.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk in minimal amounts.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: NICE NG240; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Allergic reactions, Dystonic reactions.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 25–50 mg IV/IM/PO q4-6h (max 400 mg/day).

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 1 mg/kg IV/PO q6h (max 50 mg/dose).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]CNS Depressants:[/b] Additive sedation.
• [b]MAOIs:[/b] Prolonged anticholinergic effects.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Drowsiness, dizziness.
• Dry mouth, blurred vision.
• Paradoxical excitation (children).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Do NOT use as a substitute for adrenaline in anaphylaxis.[/color]
• Avoid in neonates.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Use with caution.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF; Resuscitation Council UK.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Allergic reactions.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 10–20 mg IV/IM slowly (max 40 mg/day).

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.35 mg/kg/day divided into 4 doses.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]CNS Depressants:[/b] Additive sedation.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Drowsiness, dizziness.
• Dry mouth, blurred vision.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]Avoid in neonates and premature infants.[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Use with caution.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Status Epilepticus, Sedation.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Status Epilepticus:[/b] 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg).
• [b]Sedation:[/b] 1–2 mg IV slowly.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Status Epilepticus:[/b] 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]Opioids / CNS Depressants:[/b] Severe respiratory depression and coma.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Respiratory depression, apnea.
• Hypotension.
• Sedation, confusion.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]High-alert medication. Have bag-mask ventilation ready.[/color]
• Flumazenil is the antidote.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category D. Risk of fetal malformations (cleft lip/palate).
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: NCS Status Epilepticus Guideline; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Rapid Sequence Intubation (RSI).

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.3 mg/kg IV bolus (usually 20 mg).

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.3 mg/kg IV bolus.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]Other CNS depressants:[/b] Additive sedation.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Adrenal suppression (transient).
• Myoclonus.
• Nausea, vomiting.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]Do NOT use in septic shock (adrenal suppression worsens mortality).[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: Difficult Airway Society Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] ICU Sedation.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Loading:[/b] 1 mcg/kg IV over 10 mins (optional).
• [b]Maintenance:[/b] 0.2–0.7 mcg/kg/hour IV infusion.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Maintenance:[/b] 0.2–0.7 mcg/kg/hour IV infusion.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Anesthetics / Opioids / Benzodiazepines:[/b] Additive sedative effects.
• [b]Beta-blockers:[/b] Additive bradycardia.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Bradycardia, hypotension.
• Hypertension (transient).
• Dry mouth, nausea.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Monitor heart rate and BP continuously.[/color]
• Avoid in advanced heart block.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: ICU Sedation Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Rapid Sequence Intubation (RSI), Muscle relaxation.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]RSI:[/b] 1–1.2 mg/kg IV push.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]RSI:[/b] 1.2 mg/kg IV push.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Aminoglycosides / Magnesium:[/b] Enhance neuromuscular blockade.
• [b]Phenytoin:[/b] May decrease the effect.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Prolonged paralysis.
• Anaphylaxis (rare).
• Tachycardia, hypertension (mild).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Prolonged paralysis in renal or hepatic failure.[/color]
• Ensure sedation is adequate.
• [b]Antidote:[/b] Sugammadex or Neostigmine.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Used in C-section.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: Difficult Airway Society; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Rapid Sequence Intubation (RSI).

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]RSI:[/b] 1–1.5 mg/kg IV push.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]RSI:[/b] 2 mg/kg IV push.
[color=#991B1B]CONTRAINDICATED in children with unknown neuromuscular disease.[/color]

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Digoxin:[/b] Increased risk of arrhythmias.
• [b]Non-depolarizing muscle relaxants:[/b] Antagonize effect.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Hyperkalemia (can cause fatal cardiac arrest).
• Malignant hyperthermia.
• Bradycardia (children with repeated doses).
• Muscle fasciculations.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]CONTRAINDICATED in major burns, crush injuries, spinal cord injury (after 24-48h), or hyperkalemia.[/color]
• Avoid in personal/family history of malignant hyperthermia.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Used in C-section.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: AHA 2025; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Opioid Overdose.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.04–0.4 mg IV, titrate every 2-3 mins to RR > 12/min.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 2 mg).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]Opioids:[/b] Directly antagonizes their effect.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Acute opioid withdrawal (agitation, tachycardia, hypertension).
• Pulmonary edema (rare).
• Seizures (rare).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Short half-life (30-90 mins). Patients may re-sedate after drug wears off.[/color]
• Can precipitate fatal withdrawal in opioid-dependent neonates.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Use with caution in opioid-dependent mothers.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: AHA 2025; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Benzodiazepine Overdose.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.2 mg IV over 15 seconds. Repeat 0.3 mg, then 0.5 mg every 1 min (max 3 mg).

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.01 mg/kg (max 0.2 mg).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Benzodiazepines:[/b] Antagonizes their effect.
• [b]TCAs:[/b] Flumazenil can induce seizures in mixed TCA/benzo overdose.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Seizures (especially in mixed overdose).
• Acute withdrawal syndrome.
• Nausea, vomiting.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]CONTRAINDICATED in TCA overdose or chronic benzodiazepine users (risk of fatal seizures).[/color]
• Short half-life - patients may re-sedate.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Not recommended.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF; Toxicology Guidelines.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 500–1000 mg every 4-6 hours (max 4 g/24h).
