[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 15 mg/kg every 4-6 hours (max 60 mg/kg/day).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Warfarin:[/b] Regular high-dose can increase INR.
• [b]Alcohol:[/b] Increases risk of hepatotoxicity.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Hepatotoxicity (in overdose).
• Nausea, rash (rare).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]STRICT MAXIMUM DOSE: 4 g/day (reduce to 2-3 g in liver disease or alcoholics).[/color]
• Antidote: N-Acetylcysteine.
• Check total dose in combination products.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Safest analgesic in pregnancy.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk in small amounts. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Moderate to severe pain.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 50–100 mg every 4-6 hours (max 400 mg/day).

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 1–2 mg/kg (max 100 mg/dose). [color=#991B1B]Not recommended < 12 years.[/color]

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]SSRIs / SNRIs / MAOIs:[/b] Risk of Serotonin Syndrome.
• [b]Benzodiazepines:[/b] Severe respiratory depression.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, drowsiness.
• Seizures (lowers seizure threshold).
• Serotonin syndrome.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Avoid in patients with epilepsy.[/color]
• High risk of dependence.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Crosses placenta.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Avoid.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Acute Agitation/Psychosis, Delirium.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 2–5 mg IV/IM (max 20 mg/day).

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.01–0.05 mg/kg (specialist use).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]QT-prolonging drugs:[/b] Additive QT prolongation.
• [b]CNS Depressants:[/b] Additive sedation.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS).
• QT prolongation, Torsades.
• Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]High risk of QT prolongation (monitor ECG).[/color]
• Have Diphenhydramine ready for acute dystonia.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Risk of neonatal EPS.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF; ICU Delirium Guidelines.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Nausea and Vomiting.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 4–8 mg IV/PO every 8-12 hours.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.1–0.15 mg/kg IV/PO (max 4 mg per dose).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]QT-prolonging drugs:[/b] Additive QT prolongation.
• [b]Apomorphine:[/b] Severe hypotension.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Headache, constipation.
• QT prolongation.
• Transient elevation in liver enzymes.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]QT prolongation (monitor ECG in high-risk patients).[/color]
• Single IV dose > 16 mg is contraindicated.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Safe for hyperemesis gravidarum.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk in small amounts.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Nausea/Vomiting, Gastroparesis.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 10 mg IV/IM/PO every 8 hours.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.1–0.15 mg/kg every 8 hours.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Anticholinergics:[/b] Antagonize the prokinetic effect.
• [b]Antipsychotics:[/b] Increased risk of EPS.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Extrapyramidal symptoms (acute dystonia).
• Restlessness (akathisia).
• Hyperprolactinemia.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]High risk of acute dystonic reactions. Have Procyclidine ready.[/color]
• Do NOT use for more than 5 days.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Safe.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Status Epilepticus, Seizure prophylaxis.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Status Epilepticus:[/b] 60 mg/kg IV (max 4500 mg) over 15 mins.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 40–60 mg/kg IV (max 4500 mg) over 15 mins.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • Minimal drug interactions compared to older antiepileptics.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Somnolence, dizziness, fatigue.
• Behavioral changes (irritability, aggression).
• Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (rare).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Requires dose adjustment in renal impairment.[/color]
• Do not stop abruptly.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk in small amounts.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: NCS Status Epilepticus Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Status Epilepticus.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 20 mg/kg IV (max 1500 mg) at max rate 50 mg/min.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 20 mg/kg IV (max 1500 mg) at max rate 1–3 mg/kg/min.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Warfarin:[/b] Alters anticoagulant effect.
• [b]Corticosteroids:[/b] Reduces steroid effect.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Hypotension, bradycardia, arrhythmias.
• Nystagmus, ataxia.
• Purple glove syndrome.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]MUST dilute in 0.9% Saline ONLY (precipitates in Dextrose).[/color]
• Do NOT give faster than 50 mg/min.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category D. Fetal hydantoin syndrome.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: NCS Status Epilepticus Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Status Epilepticus.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 20 mg PE/kg IV (max 1500 mg PE) at max rate 150 mg PE/min.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 20 mg PE/kg IV (max 1500 mg PE) at max rate 3 mg PE/kg/min.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • Same as Phenytoin.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Paresthesias, pruritus.
• Hypotension, bradycardia.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Dosing is in Phenytoin Equivalents (PE).[/color]
• Can be diluted in D5W or NaCl.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category D. Same risks as Phenytoin.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: NCS Status Epilepticus Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Status Epilepticus, Bipolar disorder.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Status Epilepticus:[/b] 40 mg/kg IV (max 3000 mg) over 10 mins.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 40 mg/kg IV (max 3000 mg).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Lamotrigine:[/b] Increases risk of severe rash.
• [b]Carbapenems:[/b] Reduce valproate levels drastically.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Hyperammonemia, hepatotoxicity.
• Pancreatitis.
• Thrombocytopenia.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]Highly teratogenic (neural tube defects). Contraindicated in women of childbearing potential unless essential.[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category D (highly teratogenic).
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: NCS Status Epilepticus Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Raised Intracranial Pressure (ICP).

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.25–1 g/kg IV over 20 mins.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 0.25–1 g/kg IV over 20 mins.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]Nephrotoxic drugs:[/b] Increased risk of AKI.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Fluid overload, pulmonary edema.
• Hypernatremia.
• Acute Kidney Injury.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Use an in-line filter (crystallization can occur).[/color]
• Monitor electrolytes and osmolality.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BTF Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Severe symptomatic hyponatremia, Raised ICP.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Hyponatremia:[/b] 100–150 mL IV over 20 mins.
• [b]Raised ICP:[/b] 250 mL IV bolus.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 2.5–5 mL/kg IV over 15-20 mins.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]Other sodium-containing fluids:[/b] Additive hypernatremia.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Hypernatremia, metabolic acidosis.
• Pulmonary edema.
• Osmotic demyelination.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Central line preferred (highly irritating).[/color]
• Monitor Na+ levels every 2-4 hours.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: European Guidelines on Hyponatremia; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Prevention of cerebral vasospasm after SAH.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 60 mg PO/NG every 4 hours for 21 days.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• Not established.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]CYP3A4 inhibitors:[/b] Increase nimodipine levels (severe hypotension).
• [b]CYP3A4 inducers:[/b] Decrease nimodipine levels.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Hypotension.
• Headache.
• Reflex tachycardia.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Monitor BP closely.[/color]
• If given via NG tube, crush and extract immediately.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: AHA/ASA SAH Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Wernicke's Encephalopathy, Thiamine deficiency.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Prophylaxis:[/b] 100 mg IV/IM daily.
• [b]Encephalopathy:[/b] 500 mg IV TID for 3-5 days.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 10–50 mg IV/IM daily.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]CRITICAL: Always give thiamine BEFORE glucose in alcoholics.[/color]

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Anaphylaxis (rare).
• Local irritation.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]Must be given BEFORE glucose in alcoholics to prevent Wernicke's.[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category A. Safe.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: NICE Alcohol Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Severe infections (intra-abdominal, pneumonia, meningitis).

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Severe infection:[/b] 1 g IV every 8 hours.
• [b]Meningitis:[/b] 2 g IV every 8 hours.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 20 mg/kg IV every 8 hours (max 1 g).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]Valproate:[/b] Significantly reduces valproate levels. Avoid combination.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Seizures (especially in renal impairment).
• Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting.
• C. difficile-associated diarrhea.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Requires dose adjustment in renal impairment.[/color]
• High risk of seizures.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk in small amounts.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF; Sanford Guide.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] MRSA infections, C. difficile (oral).

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]IV:[/b] 15–20 mg/kg IV every 8-12 hours.
• [b]PO (C. diff):[/b] 125 mg PO every 6 hours.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 15 mg/kg IV every 6 hours.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Aminoglycosides:[/b] Additive nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity.
• [b]Loop diuretics:[/b] Increased risk of ototoxicity.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity.
• Red Man Syndrome.
• Phlebitis.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Infuse over at least 60 minutes to prevent Red Man Syndrome.[/color]
• Monitor trough levels (target 15-20 mcg/mL).

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk in small amounts.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: IDSA MRSA Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Anaerobic infections, C. difficile.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 500 mg IV/PO every 8 hours.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 7.5 mg/kg IV/PO every 8 hours (max 500 mg).

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Alcohol:[/b] Disulfiram-like reaction.
• [b]Warfarin:[/b] Increases INR.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Nausea, metallic taste.
• Dark urine (harmless).
• Peripheral neuropathy.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]Avoid alcohol during and for 48 hours after treatment.[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Safe in 2nd/3rd trimester.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF; Sanford Guide.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Severe gram-negative infections.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 15 mg/kg once daily IV/IM.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 15–20 mg/kg once daily.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Other nephrotoxins:[/b] Severe nephrotoxicity.
• [b]Loop diuretics:[/b] Increased ototoxicity.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Nephrotoxicity.
• Ototoxicity.
• Neuromuscular blockade.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]Monitor renal function and drug levels.[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category D. Fetal ototoxicity.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF; Sanford Guide.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Severe gram-negative infections.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 5–7 mg/kg once daily IV/IM.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 5–7.5 mg/kg once daily.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • Same as Amikacin.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content: • Nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]Monitor renal function and drug levels.[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category D. Fetal ototoxicity.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF; Sanford Guide.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Community-acquired pneumonia, Pertussis.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]IV:[/b] 500 mg daily.
• [b]PO:[/b] 500 mg day 1, then 250 mg daily.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 10 mg/kg day 1, then 5 mg/kg daily.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]QT-prolonging drugs:[/b] Additive QT prolongation.
• [b]Antacids:[/b] Reduce absorption.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Diarrhea, nausea.
• QT prolongation.
• Hepatotoxicity.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]Monitor ECG in patients with risk factors for QT prolongation.[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Safe.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF; IDSA CAP Guidelines.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Atypical pneumonia, Rickettsial infections.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 100 mg every 12 hours.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 2.2 mg/kg every 12 hours.
[color=#991B1B]Avoid in children < 8 years.[/color]

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]Antacids / Iron / Calcium:[/b] Reduce absorption.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Photosensitivity.
• Esophageal irritation.
• Teeth discoloration (children).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Avoid in pregnancy and children <8 (except life-threatening infections).[/color]
• Take with plenty of water.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category D.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF; Sanford Guide.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Anaerobic infections, MRSA skin infections.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]IV:[/b] 600–900 mg every 8 hours.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]IV:[/b] 10 mg/kg every 8 hours.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]Neuromuscular blockers:[/b] Enhances blockade.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• C. difficile-associated diarrhea (high risk).
• Diarrhea, nausea.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]High risk of C. difficile colitis.[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Safe.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF; Sanford Guide.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Intra-abdominal infections, skin infections.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 1.5–3 g IV every 6 hours.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 100–200 mg/kg/day divided q6h.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Allopurinol:[/b] Increased risk of rash.
• [b]Methotrexate:[/b] Increased toxicity.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Diarrhea, nausea.
• Rash (penicillin allergy).

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]Contraindicated in severe penicillin allergy.[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Safe.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF; Sanford Guide.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] HSV, VZV, Encephalitis.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]HSV/VZV:[/b] 5–10 mg/kg IV every 8 hours.
• [b]Encephalitis:[/b] 10 mg/kg IV every 8 hours.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Neonatal HSV:[/b] 20 mg/kg IV every 8 hours.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]Nephrotoxic drugs:[/b] Additive nephrotoxicity.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Nephrotoxicity (crystal nephropathy).
• Neurotoxicity.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Ensure good hydration.[/color]
• Infuse slowly over 1 hour.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Safe.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF; Sanford Guide.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Candida infections, Cryptococcal meningitis.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• [b]Loading:[/b] 400 mg, then 200–400 mg daily.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 12 mg/kg loading, then 6–12 mg/kg daily.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]QT-prolonging drugs:[/b] Additive QT prolongation.
• [b]Warfarin:[/b] Increases INR.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• QT prolongation.
• Hepatotoxicity.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]Monitor liver function and ECG.[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category D. High doses in 1st trimester associated with birth defects.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Excreted in breast milk. Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF; Sanford Guide.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Fluid resuscitation, Maintenance, Dilution.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 500–1000 mL IV bolus.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 10–20 mL/kg IV bolus.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]Lithium:[/b] Sodium restriction increases lithium reabsorption.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Hypernatremia, hyperchloremic acidosis.
• Fluid overload.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]Avoid in fluid overload (heart failure, renal failure).[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category A. Safe.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: NICE IV Fluids Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Fluid resuscitation, Burns, Trauma.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 500–1000 mL IV bolus.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 10–20 mL/kg IV bolus.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content:
• [b]Blood Transfusion:[/b] Contains calcium, can cause clotting (flush line).
• [b]Ceftriaxone:[/b] Avoid mixing.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Hyperkalemia (contains K+).
• Fluid overload.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Avoid in severe hyperkalemia.[/color]
• Preferred over normal saline in large-volume resuscitation.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category A. Safe.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: ATLS Guidelines; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Hypoglycemia, Maintenance fluid.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 150–200 mL IV bolus.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 2–5 mL/kg IV bolus.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]Insulin:[/b] Directly opposes the effect.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Hyperglycemia.
• Fluid overload.
• Hyponatremia.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]Do NOT use in isolation for resuscitation.[/color]
• Give thiamine first in alcoholics.

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category A. Safe.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: BNF; BSPED Guidelines.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Severe Hypoglycemia (adults only).

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 25–50 mL IV bolus.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• [color=#991B1B]CONTRAINDICATED in children (use D10W).[/color]

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]Insulin:[/b] Directly opposes the effect.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Severe tissue necrosis if extravasation.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]NEVER give to children.[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION

• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category A. Safe.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:

• [b]DKA:[/b] 0.1 unit/kg/hour IV infusion.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS

• 20–40 mmol KCl in 1 L of fluid over 1-4 hours.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]ACE inhibitors / ARBs:[/b] Increase risk of hyperkalemia.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION

• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category A. Safe.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS

sections.heading: 4. WARNING

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS

• 50 g PO/NG.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Paracetamol Overdose.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• Bag 1: 150 mg/kg over 1 hour.
• Bag 2: 50 mg/kg over 4 hours.
• Bag 3: 100 mg/kg over 16 hours.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]Nitroglycerin:[/b] NAC can potentiate hypotension.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Anaphylactoid reaction.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]High risk of anaphylactoid reactions.[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category B. Safe (do not withhold in overdose).
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Safe.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: TOXBASE; Paracetamol Overdose Guidelines.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Organophosphate Poisoning.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 1–2 g IV over 15-30 mins, then 500 mg/hour.

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 20–50 mg/kg IV over 15-30 mins, then 10–20 mg/kg/hour.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]Atropine:[/b] Synergistic effect.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Hypertension, tachycardia.
• Muscle rigidity.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]Must be given early (before 'aging' of the enzyme occurs - usually within 24-48 hours).[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: TOXBASE.

sections.heading: 1. DOSAGE AND INDICATIONS
sections.content:
[b]INDICATIONS:[/b] Iron Overdose.

[b]ADULT DOSAGE:[/b]
• 15 mg/kg/hour IV infusion (max 80 mg/kg/day).

[b]PEDIATRIC DOSAGE:[/b]
• 15 mg/kg/hour IV infusion.

sections.heading: 2. INTERACTION WITH OTHER DRUGS
sections.content: • [b]Vitamin C:[/b] Enhances iron excretion but may increase cardiac toxicity.

sections.heading: 3. ADVERSE EFFECTS
sections.content:
• Hypotension, tachycardia.
• Nephrotoxicity.

sections.heading: 4. WARNING
sections.content: • [color=#991B1B]Infuse slowly (rapid infusion causes severe hypotension).[/color]

sections.heading: 5. SAFETY IN PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
sections.content:
• [b]Pregnancy:[/b] Category C. Use only for life-threatening iron toxicity.
• [b]Lactation:[/b] Unknown.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: TOXBASE; BNF.

sections.heading: 1. RECOGNIZE CARDIAC ARREST
sections.content:
• Unresponsive.
• No normal breathing (or only gasping).
• No pulse for 10 seconds.

[color=#991B1B]Start CPR immediately.[/color]

sections.heading: 2. IMMEDIATE ACTIONS (BLS)
sections.content:
• [b]Chest Compressions:[/b] 100–120/min, depth 5–6 cm.
• [b]Airway:[/b] Head-tilt/chin-lift, bag-mask ventilation (30:2).
• [b]Attach Defibrillator/Monitor:[/b] As soon as possible.
• [b]IV/IO Access:[/b] Do not interrupt CPR.

sections.heading: 3. SHOCKABLE RHYTHM (VF/pVT)
sections.content:
• [b]Defibrillate:[/b] Biphasic 120–200 J.
• [b]CPR:[/b] Immediate 2 minutes (do not check rhythm).
• [b]Epinephrine:[/b] 1 mg IV/IO (after 2nd shock), repeat every 3-5 mins.
• [b]Amiodarone:[/b] 300 mg IV/IO (after 3rd shock), then 150 mg.
• [b]Reversible Causes:[/b] Treat 5Hs & 5Ts.

sections.heading: 4. NON-SHOCKABLE RHYTHM (Asystole/PEA)
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]DO NOT DEFIBRILLATE.[/color]
• [b]CPR:[/b] Continuous 2-minute cycles.
• [b]Epinephrine:[/b] 1 mg IV/IO as soon as possible, repeat every 3-5 mins.
• [b]Reversible Causes:[/b] Treat 5Hs & 5Ts.

sections.heading: 5. POST-ROSC CARE
sections.content:
• [b]Airway:[/b] Secure (ETT) + Capnography.
• [b]Oxygen:[/b] Target SpO2 94–98%.
• [b]Ventilation:[/b] Target PaCO2 35–45 mmHg.
• [b]Circulation:[/b] Target MAP ≥ 65 mmHg.
• [b]TTM:[/b] Targeted Temperature Management (32–36°C) if comatose.
• [b]ECG & Labs:[/b] 12-lead ECG, blood gas, lactate, electrolytes.

sections.heading: 6. DON'T MISS
sections.content:
• Do not delay defibrillation.
• Do not over-ventilate (reduces venous return).
• Do not stop CPR to check rhythm for prolonged periods.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: AHA 2025 ACLS Guidelines; ERC 2025.

sections.heading: 1. A - AIRWAY (C-SPINE)
sections.content:
• Manual in-line stabilization (MILS).
• Assess patency (speak to patient).
• Suction, airway adjuncts (OPA/NPA).
• Definitive airway (ETT) if GCS < 8.

sections.heading: 2. B - BREATHING
sections.content:
• High-flow oxygen (15 L/min).
• Auscultate (tension pneumothorax, hemothorax).
• [b]Tension Pneumothorax:[/b] Immediate needle decompression.
• [b]Open Pneumothorax:[/b] 3-sided occlusive dressing.

sections.heading: 3. C - CIRCULATION
sections.content:
• Assess pulse, BP, capillary refill.
• Stop external bleeding (pressure, tourniquet).
• 2 large-bore IVs, crossmatch blood.
• [b]Permissive Hypotension:[/b] Target SBP 80-90 mmHg (except TBI).
• [b]TXA:[/b] 1 g IV over 10 mins if within 3 hours of injury.

sections.heading: 4. D - DISABILITY
sections.content:
• GCS (Glasgow Coma Scale).
• Pupils (size, reactivity).
• Focal neurological deficit (spinal cord injury).

sections.heading: 5. E - EXPOSURE
sections.content:
• Fully undress to assess all injuries.
• [b]PREVENT HYPOTHERMIA:[/b] Warm blankets, warm fluids.
• Log-roll to examine the back.

sections.heading: 6. ADJUNCTS
sections.content:
• [b]ECG, BP, SpO2, Capnography.[/b]
• [b]Urinary & Gastric Catheters.[/b]
• [b]X-rays:[/b] Chest, Pelvis.
• [b]FAST Scan:[/b] Free fluid in abdomen/pericardium.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: ATLS 10th/11th Edition.

sections.heading: 1. GIVE OXYGEN
sections.content:
• Target SpO2 94–98% (or 88–92% if COPD).
• High-flow oxygen if hypoxemic.

sections.heading: 2. TAKE BLOOD CULTURES
sections.content:
• At least 2 sets (aerobic and anaerobic).
• Do not delay antibiotics for cultures in unstable patients.

sections.heading: 3. GIVE IV ANTIBIOTICS
sections.content:
• Broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 HOUR.
• Follow local guidelines (e.g., Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV).

sections.heading: 4. GIVE IV FLUIDS
sections.content:
• 30 mL/kg crystalloid for hypotension or lactate ≥ 4.
• Use balanced crystalloids (Ringer's Lactate) if available.
• Reassess after each bolus.

sections.heading: 5. CHECK LACTATE
sections.content:
• Measure serum lactate.
• Repeat within 2-4 hours if initial > 2 mmol/L.

sections.heading: 6. MONITOR URINE OUTPUT
sections.content:
• Insert urinary catheter.
• Target urine output ≥ 0.5 mL/kg/hour.

sections.heading: DON'T MISS
sections.content:
• Do not delay antibiotics for investigations.
• Do not miss the source (abscess, perforation, infected line).
• Escalate to ICU if patient remains hypotensive.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021; NICE NG51.

sections.heading: 1. TIME IS BRAIN
sections.content:
• Record exact time of onset (last known well).
• Goal: Door-to-needle time < 30-60 minutes.
• Exclude hypoglycemia (check glucose immediately).

sections.heading: 2. IMMEDIATE IMAGING
sections.content:
• Urgent Non-Contrast CT Head (within 20 mins).
• Exclude intracranial hemorrhage (ICH).
• CTA if Large Vessel Occlusion (LVO) suspected.

sections.heading: 3. INCLUSION & EXCLUSION
sections.content:
• [b]Window:[/b] Within 4.5 hours of onset.
• [b]BP:[/b] Must be < 185/110 mmHg (lower with Labetalol).
[color=#991B1B]Exclusions: Active bleeding, recent surgery/stroke (<3 months), platelets < 100,000, INR > 1.7 (on warfarin).[/color]

sections.heading: 4. THROMBOLYSIS DOSING
sections.content:
• [b]Alteplase:[/b] 0.9 mg/kg IV (max 90 mg).
• Give 10% as a bolus over 1 min, rest over 60 mins.
• OR [b]Tenecteplase (TNK):[/b] 0.25 mg/kg IV single bolus (max 25 mg).

sections.heading: 5. POST-THROMBOLYSIS CARE
sections.content:
• Strict BP < 180/105 mmHg for 24 hours.
• Neuro checks every 15 mins for 2 hours.
• No antiplatelets/anticoagulants for 24 hours.
• Repeat CT head if sudden deterioration (headache, vomiting, reduced GCS).

sections.heading: 6. THROMBECTOMY
sections.content:
• Indicated for Large Vessel Occlusion (LVO).
• Within 6 hours (or up to 24 hours with favorable perfusion imaging).
• Contact Interventional Radiology / Neurointervention team.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: AHA/ASA 2019/2021 Stroke Guidelines.

sections.heading: 1. IMMEDIATE ACTIONS
sections.content:
• ABCDE, hourly glucose, 2-hourly K+.
• IV access, VBG, blood ketones, U&E.
• Identify precipitant (infection, missed insulin, MI).

sections.heading: 2. FLUIDS (CRITICAL)
sections.content:
• [b]0.9% NaCl:[/b] 15-20 mL/kg in first hour (approx 1L).
• Adjust in HF/renal impairment.
• When glucose < 14 mmol/L: switch to 5% Dextrose + 0.45% NaCl.

sections.heading: 3. POTASSIUM (HOLD INSULIN IF LOW)
sections.content:
• [color=#991B1B]K+ < 3.3 mmol/L:[/color] HOLD insulin. Give IV potassium first.
• [b]K+ 3.3-5.2 mmol/L:[/b] Add 20-30 mmol KCl to each liter of fluid.
• [b]K+ > 5.2 mmol/L:[/b] Hold potassium, recheck 2-hourly.

sections.heading: 4. INSULIN INFUSION
sections.content:
• [b]Start:[/b] After K+ is safe (≥3.3) and fluids begun.
• [b]Dose:[/b] 0.1 unit/kg/hour IV infusion (no bolus).
• [b]Preparation:[/b] 50 units regular insulin in 50 mL 0.9% NaCl (1 unit/mL).
• Continue until ketones < 0.6 and pH > 7.30.

sections.heading: 5. MONITORING
sections.content:
• Hourly glucose.
• 2-hourly K+ and U&E.
• 2-4 hourly VBG.
• Hourly urine output.
• Neuro checks (cerebral edema is rare in adults).

sections.heading: 6. DON'T MISS
sections.content:
• Never start insulin if K+ < 3.3.
• Never stop insulin when glucose normalizes (add dextrose).
• Bicarbonate is not routine (only if pH < 6.9 with shock).
• Do not mistake DKA abdominal pain for surgical abdomen.

sections.heading: REFERENCES
sections.content: ADA 2024 Consensus; JBDS DKA Guidelines.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Mean arterial pressure (MAP) is the average arterial pressure throughout one cardiac cycle, important for organ perfusion.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: MAP = DBP + (SBP - DBP) / 3

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Normal: 70-100 mmHg.
Target in Sepsis/Septic Shock: ≥ 65 mmHg.
Target in TBI: ≥ 80 mmHg.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: The Shock Index is a rapid bedside tool to assess the severity of hypovolemic/hemorrhagic shock.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Shock Index = HR / SBP

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Normal: 0.5 - 0.7.
Elevated (> 0.9): Suggests significant hypovolemia/shock.
> 1.0: Severe shock, high mortality risk.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Calculates the anion gap in serum to help differentiate causes of metabolic acidosis.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Anion Gap = Na+ - (Cl- + HCO3-)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Normal: 8-12 mEq/L.
Elevated (> 12): High anion gap metabolic acidosis.
Normal: Normal anion gap (e.g., diarrhea, RTA).

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Corrects measured calcium for low albumin levels.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Corrected Ca = Measured Ca + 0.8 × (4.0 - Albumin)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Normal: 8.5 - 10.5 mg/dL.
< 8.5: Hypocalcemia.
> 10.5: Hypercalcemia.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Corrects sodium level for hyperglycemia (pseudohyponatremia).

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Corrected Na = Measured Na + 0.016 × (Glucose - 100)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
For every 100 mg/dL rise in glucose above 100, sodium falls by ~1.6 mEq/L.
Used to assess true sodium status in DKA/HHS.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Cockcroft-Gault formula to estimate creatinine clearance (CrCl) and guide drug dosing.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: CrCl = ((140 - Age) × Weight) / (72 × Creatinine) × Sex Factor

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Normal: 90-120 mL/min.
60-89: Mild impairment.
30-59: Moderate (dose adjust).
15-29: Severe.
< 15: Kidney failure.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Calculates Ideal Body Weight (IBW) using the Devine formula, essential for tidal volume calculation in mechanical ventilation.

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content: Used to calculate: Tidal volume (6-8 mL/kg IBW), Drug dosing, and Nutrition.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Calculates total fluid requirements for burn resuscitation in the first 24 hours.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Total 24h Fluid = 4 mL × Weight × %TBSA (Ringer's Lactate)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Give 50% in the FIRST 8 HOURS (from time of burn).
Give 50% in the NEXT 16 HOURS.
Target urine output: 0.5-1 mL/kg/h.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Quick SOFA score for rapid identification of sepsis at the bedside.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: qSOFA = RR ≥ 22 + SBP ≤ 100 + Altered Mentation

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Score ≥ 2: High risk of poor outcome. Further assessment needed for sepsis.
Score < 2: Sepsis still possible (qSOFA does not rule it out).

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Severity score for community-acquired pneumonia to guide admission decisions.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: CURB-65 = C + U + R + B + Age (each scored 0 or 1)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
0-1: Low risk (outpatient).
2: Moderate risk (consider admission).
3-5: High risk (admit, consider ICU if 4-5).

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Standardized scale to assess level of consciousness after acute brain injury.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: GCS = Eye + Verbal + Motor

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Severe: 3-8 (Consider intubation if ≤ 8).
Moderate: 9-13.
Mild: 14-15.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Calculates daily maintenance fluid requirements for children.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: 4 mL/kg for first 10 kg, 2 mL/kg for next 10 kg, 1 mL/kg thereafter.

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Divide by 24 for hourly rate (mL/hr).
For adolescents (>50 kg), use adult maintenance rates.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Calculates the free water deficit to guide correction of hypernatremia.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Deficit = TBW_factor × Weight × (Na / 140 - 1)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Represents the amount of fluid needed to restore normal sodium (140).
Correct slowly (max 10 mEq/L per day) to avoid cerebral edema.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Estimates the bicarbonate deficit in severe metabolic acidosis.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Deficit = 0.5 × Weight × (24 - HCO3)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Note: Routine bicarbonate use is not recommended in most cases (e.g., DKA).
Consider only in severe acidosis (pH < 7.1) or hyperkalemia.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Helps differentiate pre-renal azotemia from intrinsic renal failure (ATN).

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: FENa = (Urine Na × Serum Cr) / (Serum Na × Urine Cr) × 100

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
< 1%: Pre-renal (e.g., dehydration, heart failure).
> 2%: Intrinsic renal (e.g., ATN).
Note: Unreliable in patients on diuretics (use FEUrea instead).

General.title: Wells Score for DVT

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Clinical prediction rule for the probability of deep vein thrombosis (DVT).

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Sum of scores (Alternative diagnosis = -2)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
≤ 0: Low probability.
1-2: Moderate probability.
≥ 3: High probability.
Use with D-dimer and Ultrasound.

General.formula: cancer + paralysis + bed + tenderness + swelling + calf + edema + veins + prev + alt

General.title: Wells Score for PE

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Clinical prediction rule for the probability of pulmonary embolism (PE).

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Sum of weighted scores

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
< 2: Low probability.
2-6: Moderate probability.
> 6: High probability.
Use with D-dimer and CTPA.

General.formula: dvt + pe + hr + immob + prev + hemo + malig

General.title: CHA2DS2-VASc Score

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Estimates stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation to guide anticoagulation.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Sum of scores (Age≥75 and Stroke = 2 points each)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
0 (Male) / 1 (Female): Low risk.
1 (Male) / 2 (Female): Consider anticoagulation.
≥ 2 (Male) / ≥ 3 (Female): Oral anticoagulation recommended.

General.formula: chf + htn + age75 + dm + stroke + vasc + age65 + female

General.title: HAS-BLED Score

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Assesses the risk of major bleeding in patients on anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Sum of scores

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
0-2: Low risk.
≥ 3: High risk of bleeding (requires caution, but does NOT automatically contraindicate anticoagulation).

General.formula: htn + renal + liver + stroke + bleed + labile + elderly + drugs

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Assesses the prognosis and severity of chronic liver disease (cirrhosis).

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Sum of scores (range 5-15)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
5-6: Class A (well-compensated).
7-9: Class B (significant functional compromise).
10-15: Class C (decompensated, poor prognosis).

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Estimates the Estimated Date of Delivery (EDD) using Naegele's Rule (LMP + 280 days). Pick today's date and the first day of the Last Menstrual Period using the date selectors below.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: EDD = LMP + 280 days (40 weeks)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
The result shows:
• EDD date
• Days remaining until EDD
• Current Gestational Age

[b]Term classification:[/b]
• Preterm: < 37 weeks.
• Full term: 39–40 weeks.
• Post-term: ≥ 42 weeks.

[b]Accuracy notes:[/b]
• Naegele's rule assumes 28-day regular cycles.
• First-trimester ultrasound is more accurate if LMP is uncertain.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Calculates current Gestational Age from the Last Menstrual Period up to today. Pick today's date and the LMP date using the date selectors below.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: GA = (Today − LMP) in weeks + days

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
The result shows:
• Gestational Age in weeks + days
• Total days of pregnancy
• Calculated EDD

[b]Trimesters:[/b]
• 1st: 0–13 weeks.
• 2nd: 14–27 weeks.
• 3rd: 28+ weeks.

[b]Term classification:[/b]
• Preterm: < 37 weeks.
• Early term: 37–38 weeks.
• Full term: 39–40 weeks.
• Late term: 41 weeks.
• Post-term: ≥ 42 weeks.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Estimates weight in children aged 1-10 years using the APLS formula.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Weight = (Age + 4) × 2

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Useful in emergencies when weight is unknown.
For children < 1 year, use standard growth charts.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Estimates uncuffed endotracheal tube size for children.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Size = (Age / 4) + 4

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content: Uncuffed ETT (internal diameter in mm).

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Estimates cuffed endotracheal tube size for children.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Size = (Age / 4) + 3.5

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content: Cuffed ETT (internal diameter in mm).

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Estimates oral ETT insertion depth at the lip.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Depth (cm) = ETT Size × 3

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content: Depth at lip (cm). Confirm with capnography and chest auscultation.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: First shock energy for pediatric defibrillation.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Energy = 2 J/kg

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content: First defibrillation dose: 2 J/kg.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Subsequent shock energy for pediatric defibrillation.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Energy = 4 J/kg (max 10 J/kg or adult dose, capped at 360 J)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Second and subsequent shocks: 4 J/kg (max 10 J/kg or adult dose).
Capped at 360 J (standard adult maximum).

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Epinephrine dose for pediatric cardiac arrest (IV/IO).

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Dose = 0.01 mg/kg (max 1 mg)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Give 1:10,000 concentration. Repeat every 3-5 mins.
Volume in mL = Dose × 10 (since 1:10,000 = 0.1 mg/mL).

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: IM adrenaline dose for pediatric anaphylaxis.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Dose = 0.01 mg/kg (max 0.5 mg)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Use 1:1000 concentration (1 mg/mL).
Volume in mL = Dose (since 1:1000 = 1 mg/mL).
Alternative age-based: <6mo 150 mcg, 6mo-6yr 150 mcg, 6-12yr 300 mcg, >12yr 500 mcg.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Standard fluid bolus for pediatric resuscitation.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Volume = 20 mL/kg (10 mL/kg if cardiac)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Use 10 mL/kg in cardiac or renal disease or DKA (without shock).
Reassess after each bolus.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Tidal volume for mechanical ventilation in children.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Vt = 6 mL/kg IBW

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Lung-protective: 6 mL/kg IBW (range 5-8).
Use Ideal Body Weight, not actual.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Estimates GFR in children using the bedside Schwartz formula.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: eGFR = (0.413 × Height) / Creatinine

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Bedside Schwartz formula (2009).
Valid for children 1-16 years.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Standard vancomycin dose for pediatric severe infections (max 750 mg/dose).

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Dose = 15 mg/kg per dose (max 750 mg/dose)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Typical: 15 mg/kg q6h (max 750 mg/dose).
Adjust per renal function and levels.
Consider 60-80 mg/kg/day divided q6h for severe MRSA.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Calculates fluid deficit in pediatric dehydration.

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Deficit = Weight × %Dehydration × 10

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Give as 0.9% NaCl (or per protocol) over 24-48 hours.
Add maintenance fluids separately.

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Burn fluid resuscitation for children (per 24 hours).

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: Total = 4 × Weight × %TBSA (Ringer's Lactate)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Give 50% in first 8h, 50% in next 16h.
For children, also add maintenance fluids (Holliday-Segar).

sections.heading: DESCRIPTION
sections.content: Daily maintenance fluid (Holliday-Segar formula).

sections.heading: FORMULA
sections.content: 4 mL/kg (first 10 kg) + 2 mL/kg (next 10 kg) + 1 mL/kg (>20 kg)

sections.heading: INTERPRETATION
sections.content:
Divide by 24 for hourly rate.
Maximum 100 mL/hour in most children.
